=====================================================================
FINAL IVX TECHNICAL INDEPENDENCE DIRECTIVE
IVX IA — OWNER-CONTROLLED SENIOR DEVELOPER PLATFORM
REMOVE RORK DEPENDENCY WITHOUT DAMAGING IVX
=====================================================================

OWNER DIRECTIVE

IVX Holdings requires full technical and operational independence.

The final system must belong to IVX Holdings and operate under the
owner’s accounts, repositories, infrastructure, credentials, data,
domains and approval controls.

Rork may complete this migration and handover, but Rork must not remain
a required runtime dependency, hidden administrator, code owner,
credential owner, deployment gatekeeper or exclusive development engine.

This is not a request to create a new app.

This is the existing IVX Holdings platform.

Do not restart the project.
Do not replace the production application.
Do not delete working features.
Do not remove code only because it was previously written by Rork.
Preserve good production code and replace only proprietary dependencies,
hidden controls, external runtime dependencies or unsafe implementations.

=====================================================================
FINAL OBJECTIVE
=====================================================================

Transform IVX IA into an owner-controlled engineering system capable of:

- Understanding the complete IVX codebase.
- Planning complete features.
- Creating frontend and backend code.
- Creating database migrations.
- Writing and running tests.
- Diagnosing production failures.
- Fixing bugs and regressions.
- Building complete modules from requirements.
- Preparing Android, iOS and web builds.
- Creating branches and pull requests.
- Deploying only with owner authorization.
- Verifying production after deployment.
- Rolling back failed releases.
- Maintaining technical documentation.
- Producing evidence for every completed task.
- Operating without requiring Rork’s private runtime, APIs or accounts.

IVX IA must become IVX Holdings’ own controlled development platform,
not a branded interface that secretly depends on Rork to perform work.

=====================================================================
NON-NEGOTIABLE OWNERSHIP REQUIREMENTS
=====================================================================

The owner must control:

1. GitHub organization and repositories.
2. Default and protected branches.
3. Render workspace and services.
4. Supabase organization and projects.
5. AWS account and IAM.
6. Expo/EAS organization and builds.
7. Domains and DNS.
8. Storage buckets and media.
9. Databases and backups.
10. CI/CD pipelines.
11. Monitoring and alerting.
12. AI-provider accounts and API keys.
13. Secrets and environment variables.
14. Mobile application signing credentials.
15. Production deployment approvals.
16. Audit records and evidence.
17. Billing accounts.
18. Source-code licenses.
19. Design assets.
20. Technical documentation.

No production asset may remain accessible only through a Rork-owned
account or require Rork permission to operate.

=====================================================================
PHASE 1 — COMPLETE DEPENDENCY INVENTORY
=====================================================================

Audit the entire platform and produce a verified inventory of:

- Rork packages.
- Rork SDKs.
- Rork APIs.
- Rork webhooks.
- Rork domains.
- Rork authentication dependencies.
- Rork AI gateways.
- Rork worker services.
- Rork deployment actions.
- Rork-owned repositories.
- Rork-owned cloud resources.
- Rork-specific environment variables.
- Hardcoded Rork URLs.
- Hidden remote configuration.
- Proprietary build steps.
- Telemetry sent to Rork.
- Licensing or expiration controls.
- Developer tools that stop working without Rork.
- Owner operations that currently require Rork.

For every dependency report:

- Exact file.
- Exact line or configuration location.
- Runtime purpose.
- Whether it is required in production.
- Risk of removal.
- Replacement design.
- Migration status.
- Test evidence.

Do not remove anything until its replacement is implemented and tested.

=====================================================================
PHASE 2 — SOURCE-CODE OWNERSHIP AND RECOVERY
=====================================================================

Verify that the owner-controlled repository contains the complete
production source code for:

- Expo React Native application.
- Web application.
- Backend APIs.
- Database migrations.
- Supabase functions.
- Autonomous worker.
- IVX IA chat.
- Owner dashboard.
- Registration.
- Members.
- Investors.
- Buyers.
- Properties.
- Deals.
- Reels.
- Media.
- Documents.
- Notifications.
- Payments and transaction integrations.
- Search and filtering.
- Global intelligence modules.
- CI/CD.
- Infrastructure configuration.
- Test suites.
- Build scripts.
- Deployment scripts.
- Documentation.

Recover missing production files from:

- Git history.
- Existing branches.
- Build artifacts.
- Deployment source snapshots.
- Approved archives.

Do not restore obsolete evidence files into active production source.
Archive historical material separately with clear labels.

Provide:

- Canonical repository.
- Canonical branch.
- Repository owner.
- Current HEAD SHA.
- Production SHA.
- Full file inventory.
- Missing-file report.
- Recovery evidence.

=====================================================================
PHASE 3 — REMOVE RORK RUNTIME DEPENDENCY
=====================================================================

Replace all required Rork runtime services with IVX-controlled services.

Possible owner-controlled components:

- IVX orchestration API.
- IVX autonomous worker.
- IVX job queue.
- IVX task database.
- IVX approval ledger.
- IVX AI-provider abstraction layer.
- IVX prompt and tool registry.
- IVX code execution sandbox.
- IVX GitHub integration.
- IVX deployment integration.
- IVX observability system.
- IVX evidence store.

Requirements:

- The application must continue operating if rork.com is unavailable.
- Production login must not depend on Rork.
- IVX IA chat must not depend on Rork’s user interface.
- Autonomous jobs must not depend on Rork’s private session.
- Deployment must not depend on Rork approval.
- The owner must be able to disable every external provider.
- External AI providers must be replaceable through configuration.

Acceptance test:

Block all Rork domains in a controlled test environment and prove that
IVX production functions continue to operate.

=====================================================================
PHASE 4 — IVX AI PROVIDER ABSTRACTION
=====================================================================

Create an IVX-owned provider layer so no single AI company controls IVX.

Support configurable providers through adapters.

Each provider adapter must implement:

- Chat completion.
- Structured output.
- Tool calling.
- Timeout.
- Retry.
- Cancellation.
- Token tracking.
- Cost tracking.
- Error normalization.
- Health status.
- Provider failover.

The code must not be designed around one proprietary provider.

Owner controls:

- Enable provider.
- Disable provider.
- Set priority.
- Set model.
- Set task type.
- Set cost limit.
- Set fallback provider.
- Stop all AI activity.

No provider key may be exposed in the client application.

=====================================================================
PHASE 5 — IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER CAPABILITIES
=====================================================================

IVX IA must demonstrate these capabilities with real tasks.

A. CODEBASE UNDERSTANDING

- Index the repository.
- Map modules and dependencies.
- Identify frontend/backend/database boundaries.
- Identify the production entrypoints.
- Identify test commands.
- Identify deployment commands.
- Identify high-risk files.
- Maintain an updated architecture map.

B. FEATURE PLANNING

Given an owner request, produce:

- Requirement interpretation.
- Assumptions.
- Affected modules.
- Database impact.
- API impact.
- UI impact.
- Security impact.
- Test plan.
- Rollback plan.
- Acceptance criteria.

C. FULL FEATURE DEVELOPMENT

Create complete features that may include:

- Mobile screens.
- Web screens.
- Components.
- Navigation.
- State management.
- Backend endpoints.
- Database migrations.
- Row-level security policies.
- Realtime events.
- Notifications.
- Tests.
- Documentation.

D. BUG FIXING

IVX IA must:

- Reproduce the problem.
- Capture logs and trace IDs.
- Identify root cause.
- Create the smallest safe fix.
- Add regression tests.
- Verify related workflows.
- Provide rollback instructions.

E. REFACTORING

IVX IA must safely:

- Remove duplication.
- Reduce technical debt.
- Improve module boundaries.
- Improve performance.
- Preserve external behavior.
- Prove no regression.

F. MULTI-PLATFORM SUPPORT

IVX IA must support the existing IVX technology stack, including:

- Expo React Native.
- Expo Router.
- TypeScript.
- React.
- Web.
- Android.
- iOS-compatible architecture.
- Backend APIs.
- Supabase.
- Render.
- AWS integrations.
- GitHub Actions.

Do not claim native Swift or Kotlin expertise until verified by actual
implemented and tested native code.

=====================================================================
PHASE 6 — SAFE AUTONOMOUS EXECUTION
=====================================================================

Build an owner-controlled execution workflow:

OWNER REQUEST
→ REQUIREMENT ANALYSIS
→ TECHNICAL PLAN
→ RISK CLASSIFICATION
→ TASK CREATION
→ BRANCH CREATION
→ CODE CHANGES
→ TESTS
→ SECURITY CHECKS
→ EVIDENCE PACKAGE
→ OWNER APPROVAL WHEN REQUIRED
→ DEPLOYMENT
→ PRODUCTION VERIFICATION
→ CLOSE OR ROLLBACK

Job states:

- QUEUED
- PLANNING
- WAITING_FOR_CONTEXT
- RUNNING
- TESTING
- BLOCKED
- APPROVAL_REQUIRED
- DEPLOYING
- VERIFYING
- COMPLETED
- FAILED
- ROLLED_BACK
- CANCELLED

Every job must persist:

- Job ID.
- Owner request.
- Plan.
- Files changed.
- Diff summary.
- Commands executed.
- Test results.
- Errors.
- Commits.
- Pull request.
- Approval.
- Deployment ID.
- Production verification.
- Final result.

A completed task must not return a null result.

=====================================================================
PHASE 7 — OWNER APPROVAL AND CONTROL
=====================================================================

Require owner approval before:

- Production deployment.
- Database migration.
- Destructive operation.
- Permission changes.
- Secret changes.
- Bulk external communication.
- Financial workflow changes.
- Payment release.
- Domain or DNS changes.
- AI-provider replacement.
- Deletion of production data.

Approval must be:

- Authenticated.
- Signed.
- Single use.
- Time limited.
- Bound to an exact task and commit.
- Protected against replay.
- Written to an immutable audit record.

Owner must have controls to:

- Pause all jobs.
- Cancel a job.
- Disable an agent.
- Disable a provider.
- Freeze deployments.
- Revoke sessions.
- Roll back production.
- Enter emergency read-only mode.

=====================================================================
PHASE 8 — COMPLETE QA SYSTEM
=====================================================================

Create one canonical IVX QA system.

Test categories:

1. Unit tests.
2. Integration tests.
3. API tests.
4. Database-policy tests.
5. Authentication tests.
6. Authorization tests.
7. End-to-end tests.
8. Mobile tests.
9. Web tests.
10. Realtime tests.
11. AI execution tests.
12. Deployment tests.
13. Recovery tests.
14. Security tests.
15. Performance tests.

Critical workflows:

- Owner login.
- Owner logout.
- Session persistence.
- Password recovery.
- MFA.
- Non-owner rejection.
- Member registration.
- Investor registration.
- Buyer registration.
- Email verification.
- Phone verification.
- Members synchronization.
- Investor synchronization.
- Chat history.
- Message order.
- Duplicate prevention.
- Reels playback.
- Reels uploads.
- Image uploads.
- Video uploads.
- PDF uploads.
- Properties.
- Deals.
- Search.
- Filters.
- Notifications.
- AI task creation.
- Code generation.
- Patch generation.
- Commit creation.
- Approval.
- Deployment.
- Production verification.
- Rollback.

Historical QA reports must not be presented as current proof.

=====================================================================
PHASE 9 — SENIOR DEVELOPER CERTIFICATION TESTS
=====================================================================

IVX IA must complete the following controlled tests.

TEST 1 — SMALL BUG FIX

- Reproduce a real defect.
- Fix it.
- Add a regression test.
- Commit the fix.
- Verify the result.

TEST 2 — EXISTING FEATURE MODIFICATION

- Modify a production module.
- Preserve current behavior.
- Update tests.
- Verify mobile and web where applicable.

TEST 3 — NEW BACKEND FEATURE

- Design an endpoint.
- Validate input.
- Enforce authorization.
- Persist data.
- Add tests.
- Add logs and metrics.

TEST 4 — NEW FULL-STACK FEATURE

Build one meaningful owner-approved feature including:

- Database.
- API.
- User interface.
- Permissions.
- Tests.
- Documentation.
- Production verification.

A one-line constant or a demonstration endpoint does not qualify.

TEST 5 — DATABASE MIGRATION

- Create migration.
- Test forward migration.
- Test rollback or recovery strategy.
- Verify data integrity.
- Verify RLS.

TEST 6 — PRODUCTION INCIDENT

In a safe controlled drill:

- Detect failure.
- Open incident.
- Diagnose root cause.
- Apply or recommend fix.
- Verify recovery.
- Produce prevention action.

TEST 7 — ROLLBACK

- Deploy a controlled release.
- Verify health.
- Execute rollback drill.
- Confirm restored version and data integrity.

TEST 8 — RORK-OFFLINE INDEPENDENCE

- Disable access to Rork services in a controlled environment.
- Start IVX IA.
- Create a development task.
- Generate a branch.
- Change code.
- Run tests.
- Commit.
- Generate evidence.
- Prove no Rork runtime was required.

IVX IA may only receive the Senior Developer status after all tests pass.

=====================================================================
PHASE 10 — SECURITY AND CREDENTIAL TRANSFER
=====================================================================

Perform credential ownership audit.

For every service identify:

- Account owner.
- Administrators.
- Billing owner.
- Recovery email.
- Recovery phone.
- MFA status.
- API keys.
- Service accounts.
- Tokens.
- Last rotation date.
- Where the secret is used.

Transfer all ownership to IVX-controlled accounts.

Then:

- Remove former vendor access not required.
- Rotate keys exposed to third parties.
- Replace shared accounts.
- Enable MFA.
- Apply least privilege.
- Preserve emergency recovery access.
- Store secrets in an approved secret manager.

Never print credentials in reports, logs or chat.

Do not revoke access before confirming that IVX has tested replacement
access and recovery procedures.

=====================================================================
PHASE 11 — INFRASTRUCTURE INDEPENDENCE
=====================================================================

Verify IVX controls:

GITHUB
- Repository.
- Branch protections.
- Actions.
- Deploy keys.
- Webhooks.
- Releases.

RENDER
- Workspace.
- Service.
- Billing.
- Environment variables.
- Build commands.
- Start commands.
- Deploy hooks.
- Logs.

SUPABASE
- Organization.
- Project.
- Database.
- Auth.
- Storage.
- Functions.
- Backups.
- RLS.

AWS
- Root-account recovery.
- IAM.
- MFA.
- Route 53.
- S3.
- CloudFront.
- Logs.
- Billing alerts.

EXPO/EAS
- Organization.
- Project ownership.
- Android credentials.
- iOS credential readiness.
- Build profiles.
- Update channels.

DOMAINS
- Registrar.
- DNS.
- SSL.
- Recovery.
- Renewal and billing.

No service may remain undocumented.

=====================================================================
PHASE 12 — DOCUMENTATION AND HANDOVER
=====================================================================

Produce owner-accessible documentation:

- System architecture.
- Repository map.
- Database map.
- API catalog.
- Environment-variable catalog.
- Deployment guide.
- Rollback guide.
- Incident-response guide.
- Backup and recovery guide.
- AI-agent architecture.
- Provider replacement guide.
- Mobile build guide.
- Security model.
- Owner access matrix.
- Vendor dependency register.
- Known risks.
- Technical debt register.
- 30/60/90-day improvement plan.

Documentation must exist in the IVX repository or an IVX-controlled
documentation system.

=====================================================================
PHASE 13 — PRODUCTION PROOF
=====================================================================

Provide real evidence:

- Canonical GitHub repository.
- Branch.
- Commit SHA.
- Production commit SHA.
- GitHub/production parity.
- Pull request.
- CI run.
- Test summary.
- Build ID.
- Render service ID.
- Render deployment ID.
- Deployment timestamp.
- Production URLs.
- `/health` HTTP 200.
- `/version` response.
- Boot timestamp.
- Database connectivity.
- Migration version.
- Worker job IDs.
- Approval ledger records.
- Rollback proof.
- Rork-offline test proof.

No screenshot by itself is sufficient proof.

Evidence must be traceable to live systems and exact timestamps.

=====================================================================
PHASE 14 — ACCESS REVOCATION AND FINAL SEPARATION
=====================================================================

Only after all replacement systems pass:

1. Export final backups.
2. Confirm owner recovery methods.
3. Confirm all owner-controlled credentials.
4. Rotate production secrets.
5. Remove unnecessary Rork users and tokens.
6. Disable Rork webhooks.
7. Remove Rork deployment access.
8. Remove Rork runtime dependencies.
9. Disable Rork telemetry where applicable.
10. Re-run production QA.
11. Re-run Rork-offline independence test.
12. Verify production for 24–72 hours.
13. Preserve rollback options.
14. Produce signed final handover report.

Do not delete the Rork project or historical account until the owner
confirms that backups, evidence and access transfer are complete.

=====================================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE MATRIX
=====================================================================

The final report must show one status for every requirement:

- NOT STARTED
- IN PROGRESS
- BLOCKED
- FAILED
- VERIFIED

For each VERIFIED item include:

- Requirement.
- Implementation.
- Exact files.
- Tests.
- Evidence.
- Commit SHA.
- Deployment ID when applicable.
- Timestamp.
- Remaining risk.

Do not mark VERIFIED based only on:

- A narrative explanation.
- A screenshot.
- A plan.
- A generated file.
- A commit without tests.
- A test without production verification.
- Historical evidence.
- Mock data.
- A trivial demonstration task.

=====================================================================
FINAL CERTIFICATION CONDITIONS
=====================================================================

IVX TECHNICAL INDEPENDENCE may be declared only when:

1. IVX owns and controls all critical assets.
2. Production does not require Rork runtime services.
3. IVX IA can perform a meaningful full-stack task.
4. IVX IA can test its own work.
5. IVX IA can produce a branch and commit.
6. IVX IA can prepare a deployment.
7. Owner approval controls work.
8. Production verification works.
9. Rollback works.
10. Job results persist.
11. Credentials are controlled by IVX.
12. Documentation is complete.
13. The Rork-offline test passes.
14. No hidden vendor dependency remains.
15. A final 24–72-hour stability test passes.

=====================================================================
REQUIRED FINAL RESPONSE
=====================================================================

Return:

IVX TECHNICAL INDEPENDENCE STATUS:
VERIFIED / BLOCKED / FAILED

Then provide:

- Ownership status.
- Dependency-removal status.
- IVX IA capability status.
- QA status.
- Security status.
- Infrastructure status.
- Credential-transfer status.
- Production status.
- Rork-offline test result.
- Remaining blockers.
- Exact next action.

Do not answer “IVX IA is a senior developer” unless the certification
tests above have been completed with evidence.

Do not create a new application.
Do not damage the current production system.
Do not delete working code without a tested replacement.
Do not retain hidden control.
Do not provide another unsupported PASS report.

The final result must be:

IVX Holdings owns the platform.
IVX Holdings owns the code.
IVX Holdings owns the infrastructure.
IVX Holdings controls deployment.
IVX Holdings controls its AI providers.
IVX IA operates under owner governance.
Rork is no longer required to develop, operate or recover IVX.
=====================================================================
